Apple Brandy on the Rocks by By Kilian is a Aromatic Fruity fragrance for women and men. Apple Brandy on the Rocks was launched in 2021. The nose behind this fragrance is Sidonie Lancesseur. Top notes are Cardamom and Bergamot; middle notes are Apple, Rum, Brandy, Pineapple, Vanilla and Moss; base notes are Cedar and Ambroxan.

Makka3469 11/05/25 11:51

Apple Brandy on the Rocks opens as a watery, sweet baked apple topped with cardamom with hints of pineapple to brighten it up~ Sometimes it even comes across like caramel apples? I adore this fragrance!!

I don't get nearly as much booze as I do with Angel's Share (I'm ambivalent about this, because I love the idea of boozy scents but it can also become too heavy if not balanced just right), and it isn't woody at all on me? I'm basically getting all the sweet and fruity notes on my skin... As a gourmand and fruity scent lover, there's no way I could complain about that! Its undeniably aquatic, and its watery quality is the most defining characteristic.. The cardamom and vanilla bring back just enough warmth that it isn't truly a cold or warm fragrance? Its soooo smooth and intense enough without being overpowering on someone who prefers lighter fragrances!

Its a little aloof? Or maybe someone who seems aloof but is a big softy on closer inspection... It isn't as outwardly approachable on a lady as some of my other scents (it would probably read very approachable on a guy into aquatic frags!), but its still cozy and sweet.. It makes me feel like I'm in my own world on a wet day ^^/

Its one of my favorite snowy or rainy day scents! It could also read as a festive holiday scent, but I think its subtle enough to be worn more often than that~ It's probably too light for nighttime, but versatile enough to wear all day whether you're done up or not~

I think this perfume is somewhat unique in its own right. It's somehow boozy with an underlying freshness but also cozy at the same time and I think it's quite an undertaking to be able to combine all of these elements into a single fragrance.

There is a juiciness and subtle tartness which I presume is from the apple that permeates through the liquor tones which does feel quite complementary like a marriage between two people who are at opposing ends of the spectrum but nevertheless keep gravitating back towards eachother as if some intangible external force keeps invariably linking them back together, expertly blended in my opinion but to be patiently observed until after dry drown because this does need you to be faithful to it until the end.

Since I prefer more intimately projecting fragrances this blows Angel's Share out the park any day and feels more like something that has naturally come together in a more organic fashion.
I find it to be intricate and full of verve simultaneously which is something that I do appreciate.

JessicaLins 07/15/25 16:10

Apple Brandy on the Rocks by Kilian is a cozy, fresh fragrance that feels like a cool, crisp drink on a warm evening. It opens with a bright, juicy apple note, almost like biting into a fresh, tart apple. The brandy adds a warm, boozy depth, making it feel luxurious but still light. There's a bit of spice and wood in the background, which keeps it grounded and a little smoky, like a hint of oak from a barrel.

The scent is sophisticated but not overpowering, and it has a nice balance of sweet and fresh. It’s perfect for those who want something fresh but still a little rich and complex. The longevity is good, no beast, lasting around 6-8 hours, with decent sillage, it’s not too in-your-face but leaves a pleasant trail. It’s a great scent for autumn or evening events when you want something refreshing but with a touch of warmth…but I can use it all year long

cesardiosXO 06/26/25 21:47

Just like with Straight to Heaven yesterday, I like this way more now than when I first tried it.

First time I tried Apple Brandy On The Rocks I also hated it, and I hated it even more than Straight to Heaven because this actually smelled gross. As it dried down there was a strong, bitter and slightly mossy BO smell coming from this, and it was disgusting because it was projecting strongly off the back of my hand, so I was hit by this smell for about an hour. Now that I gave it a full wear, it is a nice scent but to be completely honest it is quite underwhelming and unremarkable. The opening smells like a freshly baked apple pie with a slight hint of cinnamon and booziness. I know cardamom is the listed spice note here, but it comes off more like cinnamon to my nose. I find the way this scent is structured to be very similar to Angels' Share, as that is a freshly baked cinnamon roll with an incredibly potent cognac note, so to me this is like an unsuccessful shuffle of Angels' Share scent profile. I'm not really a fan of apple notes in fragrances but I find this to be one of the better apple scents I've tried. It's the candied brightness of green apple that I find a bit dislikeable but here it's subdued and rounded out by the warmth of the "apple pie"-like accord and the booze. As the scent dries down it becomes softer, sweeter and especially more vanillic, I like the dry down a lot, it's very likeable.

Performance is better than Straight to Heaven, but I still find projection and sillage very underwhelming for the price. Projection is moderate and seems to go on for only about an hour or two, whereas sillage is on the light side but not as much as STH. To be fair I'm pretty anosmic to STH and not that much at all to this, so my perception is definitely skewed. Longevity is also much better, as it's been nearly 9 hours since I sprayed it on and it's still a light skin scent.

Take a moment to scroll and read MissK’s spot on review of this little Kilian masterpiece for further info.

I preferred Apple Brandy to Angel’s Share when sampling in store, so I picked it up. I was intrigued and started wearing it, but initially found it a little challenging on my skin for some reason. I’m truly not sure why. My fragrance tastes are ever evolving, so I figured I’d come back to it.

I ended up leaving this little beauty to sit in my fragrance cabinet until this past week. Now that I’m transitioning into fall mode (my favorite time of year), I was in the mood for something to start the season off right.

That said - this is magic in a bottle to me. I associate it with the fall, but I feel like this would be amazing in the winter just as well. I suppose it could be an all year fragrance, but the spiciness, opulence and warmth of it are evocative of colder weather.

As with anything, try this on skin rather than a blotter. The sort of strange, sour and chemical scent some reviewers have described is exactly what my husband experienced when wearing this. On me, though, it’s like spiced, warm apple pie (& he agrees). It’s sweet, delicious and decadent.

It starts off quite spicy and crisp in the opening. It has a freshness to it as well. Then it settles into a sweet, smooth blend of boozy apple and vanilla - among other things. It’s blended so beautifully, I can’t get enough. It’s apple done in the most sophisticated way.

This is perfection for fall. It captures the season, in my opinion. It makes me want to drink apple cider, put on a beautiful sweater & go to a fall festival. It makes an amazing date night/going out fragrance as well.

missk 07/07/24 00:40

I had never intended to sample Apple Brandy on the Rocks, as I had wanted to sample Angel's Share. Whilst at the department store, I absent-mindedly saw a bottle that resembled Angel's Share with a name starting with 'A' and spritzed away, spending the rest of the day wondering why I could smell a strong apple accord, not dissimilar to the scent of a delectable apple pie. I soon realised my mistake, and I am quite happy with my unplanned fragrance detour.

Apple Brandy on the Rocks is a sensual, apple-focused fragrance with spice, rum, cognac and syrupy vanilla. It's a very wintry, opulent and warm fragrance, synonymous with sitting cozied up by the fire with a top-shelf rum or cognac on the rocks. To my nose, it is a more refined version of Hugo Boss Boss Bottled, with a smoother apple accord that is less sharp and a less musky drydown. The fragrance overall is also sweeter, making it a perfect unisex fragrance, with a slightly gourmand approach.

This fragrances makes me think of Christmas for some reason, and this is possibly due to the boozy spice notes. The first initial spray is quite sparkling with crisp apple, pineapple, bergamot and cardamom. As the fragrance settles on the skin, the composition becomes warmer and boozier with vanilla, cedar, rum and cognac. Despite the alcohol heavy accords listed in the scent pyramid, I wouldn't say that this fragrance is overwhelming boozy. It's quite a crowd pleasing scent that leans on the sweet side.

Like most fragrances from the By Kilian line, this fragrance packs a punch, so I would recommend limiting the number of sprays. The sillage cloud is excellent, projecting more than an arm's length and the longevity is not surprisingly 8-hours plus.
